Mesillat Yesharim 19:130: For the Holy One, blessed be He, does not desire the destruction of the wicked; rather, it is a commandment incumbent upon the pious to strive to bring them merit and to atone for them.
Mesillat Yesharim 19:131: And this he must do in the intention of his service, and also actively in his prayer — namely, that he should pray for his generation, to bring atonement for whoever needs atonement, and to bring back in repentance whoever needs it, and to plead in defense of the entire generation.
Mesillat Yesharim 19:132: And they have already said, of blessed memory (Yoma 77a): concerning the verse "And I have come because of your words" (Daniel 10:12), that Gabriel did not return to enter within the Curtain except when he pleaded in defense of Israel; and to Gideon it was said (Judges 6:14): "Go in this your strength," because he had pleaded in defense of Israel.
Mesillat Yesharim 19:133: For the Holy One, blessed be He, loves only whoever loves Israel, and the more a person magnifies his love for Israel, the more the Holy One, blessed be He, magnifies His love for him.
Mesillat Yesharim 19:134: And these are the true shepherds of Israel, whom the Holy One, blessed be He, greatly desires — those who give themselves over for His flock, and seek and strive for their peace and their good in every way, and always stand in the breach to pray for them and to annul harsh decrees and to open for them the gates of blessing.
Mesillat Yesharim 19:135: To what may this be compared? To a father who loves no one more than the one whom he sees loving his children with a faithful love — this is a thing that nature itself attests to.
Mesillat Yesharim 19:136: And this is the matter of the High Priest, of whom they said (Makkot 11a): that they should have sought mercy for their generation and did not seek it. And so they said (ibid.): that man who was devoured by a lion three parasangs from Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi, and Elijah did not speak with him afterward — behold, then, the obligation incumbent upon the pious to seek mercy and to strive on behalf of the people of their generation.
Mesillat Yesharim 19:137: Now, we have already explained the primary components of piety, and their particulars are entrusted to every mind and every pure heart to conduct itself in the upright way according to these roots, each matter in its proper time.
Mesillat Yesharim 20:1:
Weighing Piety
What now needs to be explained is the weighing of this piety.
Mesillat Yesharim 20:2: And this is a matter of the utmost importance, and know truly that this is the most difficult labor within piety, for its subtlety is great, and the inclination has great entry into this matter; therefore its danger is found to be immense, for the inclination can make many good things appear as though they were evil, and many sins appear as though they were great commandments.
Mesillat Yesharim 20:3: And in truth, no person can succeed in this weighing except through three things:
Mesillat Yesharim 20:4: 1. That his heart be the most upright of hearts, so that his intention should be only to give satisfaction before Him, blessed be He, and nothing else at all.
Mesillat Yesharim 20:5: 2. And that he examine his deeds with great scrutiny, and strive to align them according to this goal.
Mesillat Yesharim 20:6: 3. And after all this, that he cast his burden upon the Lord — for then it will be said of him (Psalms 84:6,12): "Happy is the man whose strength is in You, etc. ... He will not withhold good from those who walk in innocence."
Mesillat Yesharim 20:7: However, if he lacks even one of these conditions, he will not attain perfection, and he is close to stumbling and falling — that is, if his intention is not choice and pure, or if he grows lax in the reflection that he could have made, or if, after all this, he does not place his trust in his Maker, it will be hard for him not to fall.
Mesillat Yesharim 20:8: But if he keeps all three properly — wholeness of thought, reflection, and trust — then he will truly walk securely and no evil will befall him. This is what Hannah said in her prophecy (I Samuel 2:9): "He will guard the feet of His pious ones." And David likewise said (Psalms 37:28): "and He will not forsake His pious ones; they are preserved forever."
Mesillat Yesharim 20:9: Now, what must be understood is that the words concerning piety should not be judged by their first appearance; rather, one must examine and reflect on how far the consequences of the deed reach, for sometimes the deed itself appears good, but because its consequences are evil, it must be set aside — and were one to perform it, he would be a sinner, not a pious man.
Mesillat Yesharim 20:10: Behold, the deed of Gedaliah ben Achikam is revealed to our eyes — that because of his excessive piety, in not wishing to judge Ishmael unfavorably, or not wishing to accept an evil report, he said to Yochanan ben Kareach, "You speak falsely about Ishmael" (Jeremiah 40:16). And what did this cause? It caused his own death, and the scattering of Israel, and the extinguishing of their remaining ember. And Scripture already attributes the killing of the men who were killed to him, as though he himself had killed them, as our Sages, of blessed memory, said (Niddah 61a) on the verse, "all the corpses of the men whom he had struck down by the hand of Gedaliah" (Jeremiah 41:9).
Mesillat Yesharim 20:11: And the Second Temple, too, was destroyed because of such piety, which was not weighed in the scale of righteousness, in the incident of Kamtza and Bar Kamtza. They said (Gittin 56a): the Sages considered killing him, but Rabbi Zechariah ben Avkulas said to them: people will say that one who blemishes sacrifices is put to death. They considered offering him up, but Rabbi Zechariah ben Avkulas said to them: people will say that blemished animals may be offered up on the altar.
Mesillat Yesharim 20:12: Either way, that wicked man went and slandered Israel; the Emperor came and destroyed Jerusalem. This is what Rabbi Yochanan said about this: the excessive scrupulousness of Rabbi Zechariah destroyed our house, burned our Temple, and exiled us among the nations.
Mesillat Yesharim 20:13: Behold, then, that the piety of a deed cannot be judged by that deed alone, as it stands in isolation, but one must look this way and that, in every direction that a person's mind can perceive, until he can truly judge which is more fitting — the deed or the abstention from it.
Mesillat Yesharim 20:14: Behold, the Torah commanded (Leviticus 19:17): "you shall surely rebuke your fellow" — yet how many times does a person come to rebuke sinners in a place or at a time when his words will not be heeded, causing them instead to break out even further in their wickedness, and to desecrate the Name of the Lord by adding transgression to their sin? Behold, in such a case it is not piety, but rather silence, that is called for. And so they said, of blessed memory (Yevamot 65b): just as it is a commandment to say a word that will be heeded, so it is a commandment not to say a word that will not be heeded.
Mesillat Yesharim 20:15: See, it is obvious that it is proper for every person to be first and to run for a matter of a commandment, and to strive to be among those who occupy themselves with it. However, sometimes strife can arise from this, such that the commandment itself becomes further disgraced, and the Name of Heaven becomes more desecrated through it than honored; in such a case, the pious person is certainly obligated to abandon the commandment and not pursue it.
Mesillat Yesharim 20:16: And so they said, of blessed memory, concerning the Levites, in these words (Bamidbar Rabbah 5:1): because they knew that whoever carried the Ark received a greater reward, they would abandon the table, the menorah, and the altars, and all of them would run to the Ark to take the reward; and because of this, one would quarrel, saying, "I will carry here," and another would quarrel, saying, "I will carry here," and because of this they came to behave with levity, and the Divine Presence would strike them, etc.
Mesillat Yesharim 20:17: Behold, a person is obligated to observe all the commandments in all their fine details before whoever it may be, and neither fear nor be ashamed; and so it says (Psalms 119:46): "and I will speak of Your testimonies before kings, and will not be ashamed"; and so we learned: be bold as a leopard, etc. (Avot 5:20).
Mesillat Yesharim 20:18: However, even here a distinction and discernment are needed, for all this was said concerning the essential body of the commandments, in which we are absolutely obligated, and regarding which one should set his face like flint.
Mesillat Yesharim 20:19: But there are certain additional practices of piety which, if a person were to perform them before the masses of the people, they would laugh at him and mock him, and would thereby become sinners and be punished on his account, when he could have refrained from doing those things, since they are not an absolute obligation — in such a case it is certainly more fitting for the pious person to refrain from doing them than to do them. This is what is said (Micah 6:8): "and walk humbly with your God." And many great pious ones refrained from their pious practices while in the midst of the masses of the people, because it would appear as arrogance.
Mesillat Yesharim 20:20: The general rule of the matter: whatever is essential in the commandment, he should perform even before every mocker; but whatever is not essential and causes laughter and mockery, he should not perform.
Mesillat Yesharim 20:21: You thus learn that whoever wishes to practice true piety must weigh all his deeds according to the consequences that follow from them, and according to the conditions attending them, according to the time, the company, the subject, and the place; and if abstention will bring about a greater sanctification of the Name of Heaven and satisfaction before Him than the deed, he should abstain and not do it.
Mesillat Yesharim 20:22: Or if one deed appears good but is evil in its consequences or its conditions, and another deed appears evil but is good in its consequences, everything follows the outcome and the consequence, which is truly the fruit of deeds.
Mesillat Yesharim 20:23: And these matters are entrusted only to an understanding heart and sound intellect, for it is impossible to explain all the particulars, which have no end, and "the Lord gives wisdom; out of His mouth come knowledge and understanding" (Proverbs 2:6).
Mesillat Yesharim 20:24: And the incident of Rabbi Tarfon proves this (Berachot 10b): that he was stringent, inclining toward the House of Shammai, and they said to him, You deserved to be liable for your own life, for you transgressed the words of the House of Hillel — even though he was being stringent.
Mesillat Yesharim 20:25: This is because the matter of the dispute between the House of Shammai and the House of Hillel was a grave matter for Israel, because of the great dispute that grew between them, and in the end it was determined that the halachah always follows the House of Hillel.
Mesillat Yesharim 20:26: Behold, the preservation of the Torah requires that this final ruling remain in full force forever and for all eternity, and never be weakened in any way, so that the Torah should not become, God forbid, like two Torahs; and therefore, according to this teaching, it is more pious to hold by the House of Hillel even leniently than to be stringent according to the House of Shammai. And this should be before our eyes, to see which path truly and faithfully leads to light, in doing what is upright in the eyes of the Lord.
Mesillat Yesharim 21:1:
The Ways of Acquiring Piety
Now, among the things that greatly help in acquiring piety is great contemplation and much reflection; for the more a person reflects on the greatness of His majesty, blessed be He, and the ultimate degree of His perfection, and the vast, immeasurable distance between His greatness and our lowliness, the more this will cause him to be filled with fear and trembling before Him.
Mesillat Yesharim 21:2: And in reflecting on the abundance of His kindnesses to us, and on the greatness of His love, blessed be He, for Israel, and on the closeness of the upright to Him, and on the greatness of the Torah and the commandments, and similar reflections and studies, a powerful love will certainly burn within him, and he will choose and long to cleave to Him; for upon seeing that the Name, blessed be He, is truly a Father to us, and has compassion on us as a father on his children, the will and the longing will be aroused within him to repay Him as a son to his father.
Mesillat Yesharim 21:3: And for this, a person needs to be solitary in his own chambers, and to gather all his knowledge and understanding for contemplation and reflection on these true matters.
Mesillat Yesharim 21:4: And certainly what will help him in this is much persistence and reflection upon the psalms of King David, peace be upon him, and contemplating their statements and their meaning, for since they are all filled with love, fear, and every kind of piety, upon reflecting on them, he will not fail to be greatly aroused to follow in his footsteps and walk in his ways. And likewise, reading the accounts of the deeds of the pious in the aggadot that recorded them will be helpful, for all these arouse the mind to take counsel and to act as they did in their beloved deeds; and this is clear.
Mesillat Yesharim 21:5: But the things that undermine piety are preoccupations and worries, for when the mind is preoccupied and hurried by its worries and its business dealings, it is impossible for it to turn to this reflection, and without reflection one cannot attain piety; and even if he has already attained it, these preoccupations force themselves upon the mind and confuse it, and do not allow it to grow strong in fear and love and the other matters pertaining to piety, as I have mentioned. Therefore they said, of blessed memory (Shabbat 30b): the Divine Presence rests neither in the midst of sadness, etc.
Mesillat Yesharim 21:6: All the more so pleasures and delights, which are truly the very opposite of piety, for they entice the heart to be drawn after them, and it turns away from all matters of abstinence and true knowledge.
